title: Rewrite Epic-7 dashboard tests whose bodies don't exercise the behavior their titles claim

evidence.quote: test('points summary is excluded from state when userMode is adult', () {
// This tests the invalidation pattern — in the real app, ref.invalidate()

/// Mirror of the private `_trimSederFromBreadcrumb` function in
    /// `active_track_card.dart`. Kept here as a pure-logic unit test...

why: 'points summary is excluded from state when userMode is adult' never touches the dashboard provider or screen that decides whether to render PointsSummaryWidget for a given mode — it only checks ProfileMode.adult != ProfileMode.child, true by enum definition regardless of any dashboard logic. 'pull-to-refresh triggers provider invalidation pattern' never calls ref.invalidate() or touches any Riverpod provider — it calls the pure CrossCurriculumAggregator.aggregate() function twice with different literal inputs, which trivially returns different output. If the dashboard's actual mode-gating logic or its pull-to-refresh/ref.invalidate() wiring regresses, neither test detects it, despite both titles claiming to cover exactly that.
recommendation: Either move these under a widget/provider test that pumps the real dashboard screen or provider and drives the claimed interaction (mode gating via ConsumerWidget + ProviderScope, or ref.invalidate() via the actual pull-to-refresh callback), or rename the tests to describe what they actually verify (enum comparison, aggregator purity) so the suite stops overstating its coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Test titled around dashboard/provider behavior drives that behavior directly, or is renamed to match what it verifies
mergedFrom: Test breadcrumb trimming through the real _trimSederFromBreadcrumb, not a hand-copied mirror
